title: DocAtlas image and tree ablation drops identify information availability and indexing value, not a new self-evolution mechanism
dead_end_scope: The standalone claim that DocAtlas's performance drops after removing layout/cropped images or tree annotations establish a new memory/self-evolution mechanism merely because the mutable system outperforms these component ablations.

fresh_phenomenon_closure.closure_scope: the layout/cropped-image removal and tree-annotation removal ablation drops only

counter_explanation.statement: The two ablations remove ordinary information resources rather than isolating a new self-evolution primitive. Layout images and cropped sub-images supply task-relevant visual evidence for figures, charts, and spatial document structure; removing them directly reduces observability/evidence sufficiency. Tree annotations are part of DocAtlas's mutable search/index representation and alter the information available to later retrieval; removing them degrades All-Hit and page-F1 as expected when an index/search state loses structured navigation signals. These effects are fully expressible by information availability, retrieval/index quality, and observability baselines unless information content and query budget are matched while only the evolving representation changes.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: With model and query fixed, removing task-relevant visual evidence should reduce performance most on visually grounded questions, and removing structured index/navigation state should reduce retrieval recall/precision. Both effects can be large without implying a distinct self-evolution mechanism.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: A component that exposes additional task evidence or improves search/index state can improve an agent through ordinary observability and retrieval quality; component-removal drops are not evidence of a new evolving-memory mechanism unless the same information and search budget are preserved.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: Reopen only with a preregistered same-information comparison that preserves the same visual/document evidence, query budget, and candidate pages while changing only the mutable memory/index representation, and shows a held-out decision or retrieval residual beyond information sufficiency, observability, indexing/search quality, and ordinary active-retrieval baselines. Do not reopen from another missing-modality or missing-index ablation.
counter_explanation.scope: DocAtlas arXiv:2608.07527, especially the layout-image/crop and mutable-tree ablations.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: The image ablation preserves all task evidence and only changes memory formatting: false; it removes layout images/cropped visual evidence used by figure/chart questions.
The tree ablation changes only a cosmetic note format: false; the reported raw-search All-Hit and page-F1 changes show that it changes later retrieval/index behavior.
Large component ablation drops identify a self-evolution interaction: false; the cited ablations do not match information content or estimate a factorial interaction.
The closure says mutable document memory is useless: false; it closes only a standalone novelty claim from these information-removal ablations.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen only with a same-information, matched-search-budget comparison that holds document/visual evidence and candidate support fixed while varying the evolving memory/index representation, and yields a repeatable held-out residual beyond information sufficiency, observability, retrieval/index quality, and active-search baselines.

scientific_interpretation.safe_claim: DocAtlas's ablations show that visual evidence and structured mutable indexing are useful. Those drops are already predicted by ordinary information-availability and search-quality principles and do not by themselves identify a new self-evolution mechanism.
